headline: 136 lives lost in August as measles resurges in Bangladesh
summary: Cases, hospitalisations, and deaths rose in August after a brief decline, putting additional pressure on healthcare facilities already strained by dengue.
details: Bangladesh's measles situation took a worrying turn in August, with cases, hospitalisations, and deaths all rising. The daily average of deaths shot up from 3.84 to 4.39 per day during the month.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), 32,934 cases were recorded in August, up from 31,327 in July. Hospital admissions also increased, with 27,458 patients admitted in August compared to 26,360 in July.

The resurgence is occurring while the country is facing a growing number of dengue cases, further straining healthcare facilities. Currently, over 7,700 patients are being treated for both diseases in hospitals.
Public health experts blame the surge in cases among children under six months, who are ineligible for vaccination, and gaps in vaccination coverage for older children.

The government had launched an emergency vaccination campaign in April, vaccinating 1.84 crore children. However, a gap of 38.83 lakh children was identified between Vitamin A capsule distribution and measles vaccination coverage.
Health authorities are now procuring more vaccines and planning a short, intensive programme to cover the remaining children to contain the outbreak.
Epidemiologist Prof Mahmudur Rahman suggests the government form an expert group to identify geographical and socioeconomic gaps in coverage and implement targeted interventions.
Experts also call for stronger public health measures, including isolating children with fever, wearing masks, and practicing handwashing to prevent further transmission.

136 children died in August alone as measles cases surge again in Bangladesh. Healthcare systems are under double pressure from dengue.

Bangladesh's measles situation took a worrying turn in August, with cases, hospitalisations, and deaths all rising. The daily average of deaths shot up from 3.84 to 4.39 per day during the month.

According to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), 32,934 cases were recorded in August, up from 31,327 in July. Hospital admissions also increased, with 27,458 patients admitted in August compared to 26,360 in July.

The resurgence is occurring while the country is facing a growing number of dengue cases, further straining healthcare facilities. Currently, over 7,700 patients are being treated for both diseases in hospitals.

Public health experts blame the surge in cases among children under six months, who are ineligible for vaccination, and gaps in vaccination coverage for older children.

The government had launched an emergency vaccination campaign in April, vaccinating 1.84 crore children. However, a gap of 38.83 lakh children was identified between Vitamin A capsule distribution and measles vaccination coverage.

Health authorities are now procuring more vaccines and planning a short, intensive programme to cover the remaining children to contain the outbreak.

Epidemiologist Prof Mahmudur Rahman suggests the government form an expert group to identify geographical and socioeconomic gaps in coverage and implement targeted interventions.

Experts also call for stronger public health measures, including isolating children with fever, wearing masks, and practicing handwashing to prevent further transmission.

headline: 18,000 customers seek 1,300 crore BDT refund from Sammilito Islami Bank
summary: Customers of five merged banks have begun applying for fund withdrawals, with payments scheduled to start on September 7.
details: On the first day of applications, 18,000 customers applied to withdraw their funds from Sammilito Islami Bank, requesting a total of 1,300 crore BDT.
The bank was formed by merging five distressed Islamic banks: Exim Bank, Social Islami Bank, First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank, and Union Bank.
According to Bangladesh Bank guidelines, individual depositors can withdraw the principal amount from their current, savings, and fixed deposit accounts.
However, depositors will not receive any profit earned or accrued on these deposits under this specific withdrawal facility.
If a customer withdraws the principal amount, it will be treated as a full and final settlement of that deposit.
Any existing loans or liabilities the customer has with the transferring bank will be adjusted against the deposit amount before the refund is issued.
Customers who choose not to withdraw their funds now can continue to earn profit at the applicable rates according to their original contracts.
If a fixed deposit is broken before maturity, the principal will be returned, but no profit will be paid on that amount. Partial withdrawals will still allow profit on the remaining balance.
The bank is currently verifying applications, and payments to customers are expected to begin on September 7.
caption:
18,000 customers requested 1,300 crore BDT in a single day. The rush for refunds has begun at Sammilito Islami Bank.

On the first day of applications, 18,000 customers applied to withdraw their funds from Sammilito Islami Bank, requesting a total of 1,300 crore BDT.

The bank was formed by merging five distressed Islamic banks: Exim Bank, Social Islami Bank, First Security Islami Bank, Global Islami Bank, and Union Bank.

According to Bangladesh Bank guidelines, individual depositors can withdraw the principal amount from their current, savings, and fixed deposit accounts.

However, depositors will not receive any profit earned or accrued on these deposits under this specific withdrawal facility.

If a customer withdraws the principal amount, it will be treated as a full and final settlement of that deposit.

Any existing loans or liabilities the customer has with the transferring bank will be adjusted against the deposit amount before the refund is issued.

Customers who choose not to withdraw their funds now can continue to earn profit at the applicable rates according to their original contracts.

If a fixed deposit is broken before maturity, the principal will be returned, but no profit will be paid on that amount. Partial withdrawals will still allow profit on the remaining balance.
